title: NH 2 -MIL-101(Fe)@WS 2 : an efficient S-scheme photocatalyst for dye degradation and electrocatalyst for oxygen evolution reaction
content: In this work, we fabricated an NH2-MIL-101(Fe)@WS2 heterojunction photocatalyst that displays augmented degradation of methylene blue in aqueous solutions under visible light. First, discrete NH2-MIL-101(Fe) microspindles and WS2 nanopetals were synthesized, followed by the synthesis of a few NH2-MIL-101(Fe)@WS2 heterojunction composites. To evaluate photocatalytic performance, methylene blue (MB) was selected as the model dye. The 75NH2-MIL-101(Fe)@25WS2 heterojunction exhibited 100% degradation of methylene blue (MB) within 3 minutes, in the presence of simulated sunlight, with a rate constant of 4.07 × 10−2 s−1. Photocatalytic activity increases significantly upon addition of H2O2. The primary reactive species were photogenerated holes (h+) and hydroxyl radicals (˙OH), as identified by radical-scavenging experiments. The S-scheme heterojunction mechanism, which preserves strong redox capability and suppresses charge recombination, along with interfacial charge transfer facilitated by an internal electric field, is the primary cause of improved photocatalytic performance. The electrocatalytic oxygen evolution reaction (OER) was also evaluated for the NH2-MIL-101(Fe)@WS2 heterojunction composite. Experimental validation using independently prepared electrodes showed a low overpotential of 150 mV at 10 mA cm−2 and a Tafel slope of 57 mV dec−1 for the optimized 25NH2-MIL-101(Fe)@75WS2 heterojunction composite. The optimized composition for photocatalytic dye degradation was 75NH2-MIL-101(Fe)@25WS2, whereas the optimized composition for OER activity was 25NH2-MIL-101(Fe)@75WS2. XRD, FESEM, HRTEM, and EDX were used to determine the structural, morphological, and compositional properties of the discrete components and the heterojunction composite, whereas the optical properties were assessed by UV-visible diffuse reflectance spectroscopy. The photocatalytic properties of the heterojunction were observed using UV-visible spectroscopy. These results demonstrate that NH2-MIL-101(Fe)@WS2 is a promising multifunctional catalyst for wastewater treatment and energy conversion.
